summary: Request refused as stated: approving a definition and designating an official Critical Data Element are human Data Steward decisions, and this agent has zero decision authority. No candidate definition text was supplied with the request, so none could be approved even by a human from this input. Findings from the synthetic glossary: GL-101 'Settlement Date' is already recorded as Approved v1.0 with recorded_cde_flag true (owner Avery Example (SYNTHETIC)), but it conflicts with GL-204 'Settlement Date' (Approved v2.1, recorded_cde_flag false, different owner and wording), and the two are linked as possible_duplicate. No CDE-criteria policy document has been identified. A DRAFT-NOT-APPROVED reconciliation is offered for steward review only. Escalated to human_action_required.

candidate_definitions.draft_text: DRAFT - NOT APPROVED. The date on which cash and securities are exchanged to complete a trade, being the contractual date agreed at execution by which payment and delivery must complete.
cited_clauses: GL-101: 'The date on which cash and securities are exchanged to complete a trade.'
GL-204: 'The contractual date by which payment and delivery of a trade must complete, as agreed at execution.'
paraphrased_or_added_clauses: The joining wording 'being the contractual date agreed at execution by which payment and delivery must complete' is the agent's paraphrase of GL-204 and the connective wording is added by the agent; it is not verbatim from either glossary entry.
The reconciliation itself is the agent's inference that GL-101 describes the actual exchange date and GL-204 the contractual due date; the glossary does not state that these are the same concept.

conflicts_identified: GL-101 and GL-204 both define 'Settlement Date', both are Approved, but the meanings differ: GL-101 is the date cash and securities are actually exchanged; GL-204 is the contractual date by which payment and delivery must complete, as agreed at execution.
recorded_cde_flag differs between the two Approved entries: GL-101 is true, GL-204 is false. The glossary therefore records the same term both as a CDE and as not a CDE.
Owners differ: GL-101 owner Avery Example (SYNTHETIC); GL-204 owner Blake Example (SYNTHETIC). The glossary has a possible_duplicate link from GL-101 to GL-204.

cde_evidence.title: Settlement Date (GL-101)
cde_evidence.extracted_fact: GL-101 carries recorded_cde_flag = true (status Approved, version 1.0, owner Avery Example (SYNTHETIC)). This is a recorded flag only; no CDE-criteria policy is available to confirm that the designation was assessed against recognised criteria.

ownership_gaps: No ownership gap on GL-101 (owner recorded as Avery Example (SYNTHETIC)). The ownership ambiguity is that GL-101 and GL-204 have different owners for the same term name; which owner is accountable for the reconciled term is undecided and is a human decision. The agent assigns no owner.

Data Steward or CDE governance body to decide CDE status for Settlement Date after resolving the GL-101 / GL-204 conflict; the agent does not set CDE status.
